evidence.effect_or_condition: clinical and metabolic outcomes in nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
evidence.supported_claim_language: A meta-analysis of seven randomized trials found alpha-lipoic acid did not improve liver enzymes, lipids, glycemic measures, adipocytokines, or obesity measures in NAFLD.
evidence.safety_note: The null is specific to the studied NAFLD outcomes and does not address other established or proposed uses of alpha-lipoic acid.

evidence.effect_or_condition: postoperative recovery after gastric cancer surgery
evidence.population: patients undergoing open gastrectomy for gastric cancer
evidence.supported_claim_language: In a 42-patient randomized trial, postoperative probiotics shortened hospital stay and accelerated gastrointestinal recovery, without significant inflammatory, immune, nutritional, or complication differences.
evidence.evidence_grade: randomized controlled trial; postoperative recovery signal
evidence.safety_note: The study was single-center and small, and the findings are specific to perioperative gastric-cancer care.

evidence.population: infants age 6–11 months in Nepal at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency
evidence.supported_claim_language: In a 600-infant randomized trial, daily vitamin B12 for 12 months did not reduce common infection incidence or health-clinic visits versus placebo.
evidence.evidence_grade: randomized controlled trial; infection efficacy null
evidence.safety_note: This is a secondary-outcome analysis in infants at risk of deficiency and should not be generalized to other vitamin B12 indications.

evidence.supported_claim_language: A meta-analysis of seven trials found vitamin D supplementation lowered triglycerides, while total cholesterol and LDL were not significantly changed.
evidence.safety_note: The HDL signal was regimen-dependent, and pooled results do not establish an individualized dose or broad cardiometabolic benefit.

evidence.effect_or_condition: prevention of acute respiratory infection healthcare visits in young children
evidence.study_type: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
evidence.population: pregnant women and children up to five years of age
evidence.supported_claim_language: A Cochrane review found low-certainty evidence of a slight reduction in the proportion of children with ARI-related healthcare visits, but no reduction in mean visit count.
evidence.evidence_grade: Cochrane systematic review/meta-analysis; low-certainty small prevention signal
evidence.safety_note: Higher-dose versus lower-dose vitamin D did not improve ARI visit outcomes; hypercalcemia was uncommon and evidence certainty varied.

evidence.effect_or_condition: metabolic and atherosclerosis biomarkers in epilepsy
evidence.population: adults with epilepsy receiving enzyme-inducing antiseizure medications
evidence.supported_claim_language: A small randomized trial found vitamin D increased 25(OH)D and adiponectin and reduced hs-CRP, without significant HOMA-IR or homocysteine improvement.
evidence.evidence_grade: randomized controlled trial; biomarker-specific mixed result
evidence.safety_note: The trial was small, used a specific epilepsy population, and the biomarker findings do not establish reduced cardiovascular events.

evidence.effect_or_condition: intestinal permeability and inflammation in hemodialysis
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 40-patient controlled study found three months of probiotics reduced zonulin, p-cresyl sulfate, and hs-CRP versus control in hemodialysis patients.
evidence.evidence_grade: prospective controlled clinical study; biomarker signal
evidence.safety_note: This was not described as a randomized trial and used surrogate biomarkers, so causality and clinical-outcome significance remain limited.

evidence.effect_or_condition: physiological and perceptual responses during exertional heat stress
evidence.population: young adults exercising in hot conditions
evidence.supported_claim_language: An eight-person pilot trial found berberine modestly lowered body temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, and perceived heat/exertion during exercise heat stress.
evidence.evidence_grade: randomized pilot trial; very small physiologic signal
evidence.safety_note: The sample was extremely small and the authors questioned the practical utility of the small observed changes.

evidence.effect_or_condition: strength, power, and muscular endurance in collegiate athletes
evidence.population: male NCAA Division III baseball players
evidence.supported_claim_language: A randomized crossover trial found 3 mg/kg caffeine did not improve strength, power, or muscular-endurance outcomes, and habitual use did not modify the null effect.
evidence.evidence_grade: randomized crossover trial; performance efficacy null
evidence.safety_note: This null finding is dose-, population-, and protocol-specific and should not be generalized to all caffeine performance studies.
